races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Maiden

runners_data.name: Eager Lad
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo from the A. Oliver yard (2 wins from 10 in last 14 days) with unknown going profile and no debut-run data to assess; style tagged Unknown, so watch for early positioning clues — if forward-going from the gate this course layout suits.

runners_data.name: Optics
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo whose form figures of 0-7 include a seventh at Haydock and a 13th at Hereford, suggesting limited ability so far; no going concern on turf but finishing positions point firmly to the lower end of this field.

runners_data.name: Strikepoint
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with back-to-back finishes of 10th and 7th on good ground at Goodwood, showing minimal progression; no distance or going concern, but the form gives little reason to fancy an improvement to winning level here.

runners_data.name: Beach Barbie
runners_data.note: Lynam-trained 4yo with three runs on Dundalk's synthetic surface (best finish 5th) — course-familiar but a genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear-division style is compressed into midfield by this field's make-up, meaning she races out of her comfort zone today.

runners_data.name: Famed Again
runners_data.note: Four-year-old whose recent form of 5,0,0,7,0 over 7-8f on good ground is poor, and the drop to 5f on Standard is a significant unknown; a true hold-up runner who, because the rear of the field is congested, is mapped into midfield where she is unlikely to produce her best.

runners_data.name: Forbidden
runners_data.note: The sole front runner and race-pace controller, confirmed prominent style (STYLE_FIT 0.93), but both starts at Goodwood in 2024 ended with well-beaten finishes and a flag for fading late — the key question is whether leading on Standard at Dundalk over 5f delays that fade long enough to matter.

runners_data.name: Grande Cuvee
runners_data.note: Lightly raced Heffernan/Stack 3yo whose only form includes a third at the Curragh over 5f — the relevant distance — and a ninth on soft, suggesting Standard may suit; unknown going profile but a pace-friendly style with scope for improvement.

runners_data.name: Institute
runners_data.note: Wayne Lordan takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien on a 3yo with two placed efforts over 5f and 6f on Dundalk's Standard surface — the sim-going record (1 place from 6) is modest but the prominent style and course experience are legitimate positives in this race shape.

runners_data.name: McHenry Sunrise
runners_data.note: Stack-trained 3yo flagged as a fader with a best of fourth over 5f on soft; a genuine hold-up type shuffled into midfield by the crowded rear of the field, compounding the concern that he will neither secure his position nor sustain his effort to the line.

runners_data.name: Nebrook Star
runners_data.note: Has a fourth over 5f on soft as his best effort from six starts, with limited synthetic-surface form (1 run, finished 6th); goes in blinkers (hg:b) which could sharpen early intent but the hold-up style works against him in a race where the pace will be moderate.

runners_data.name: Off We Go
runners_data.note: Hold-up 3yo from Oliver's yard wearing a hood and tongue-tie, finishing 10th and 14th at Goodwood; flagged as a fader and 35 days since last run — nothing in the form or profile suggests a change of fortune here.

runners_data.name: Osterode
runners_data.note: McCreery's lightly raced 3yo for Declan McDonogh — only one run, a fourth over 5f at the Curragh on good, which is directly relevant to today's conditions; the visor (hg:v) worn last time and the unknown scope make this one of the more intriguing unknown quantities.

runners_data.name: Tudor Flame
runners_data.note: Unraced Feane-trained 3yo carrying debut unknowns across going, style and class; same trainer as Strikepoint and listed as debutant today — the lightly raced flag and absence of any form means assessment rests entirely on market and early race behaviour.

runners_data.name: White Smoke
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on this Grassick-trained 3yo whose best effort was a fourth over 5f on good, but four subsequent runs have produced two single-figure finishes at best; a natural hold-up horse funnelled into midfield by the busy rear of the field — the booking of a top claimer is the one angle to note.

races.paceDynamic: Forbidden is the lone confirmed front runner in this 14-runner 5f maiden and should be allowed to stride to the lead unchallenged from the outset, setting a sustainable rather than scorching tempo on Standard ground at Dundalk. With no genuine rival for the early lead, Forbidden will dictate from the front and control the fractions, which on a flat 5f track creates a race where the pace is measured rather than gruelling — favouring horses who can press from just off the pace and deliver a sustained late kick rather than those relying on a true stopper's sprint. Institute, mapping as prominent, is best placed to stalk Forbidden and pounce, while Grande Cuvee and Osterode, as lightly raced unknowns, have the profile to travel well in behind a single leader. The field contains significantly more hold-up and close-up types than the race shape can accommodate — Beach Barbie, White Smoke, Famed Again and McHenry Sunrise are all genuine rear-division horses redistributed to midfield on the map; of these, White Smoke (Dylan Browne McMonagle) and Beach Barbie (Lynam yard) are most likely to jostle for a position closer to the pace than their natural style would suggest, but none of them should be trusted to reproduce their best form racing out of role. This race shape — a single, uncontested leader setting a fair tempo over a bare 5f — strongly favours horses who can track the leader from a prominent or close-mid position and produce a clean, sustained finish, making the prominent/pressing profile the most advantaged running style today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Forbidden Dictates, Pressers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Forbidden leads unchallenged and prominent/pressing horses track and pounce inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Forbidden sets a sensible tempo from the front on Standard ground, and horses settled just off the pace — Institute, Grande Cuvee, Osterode — arrive with a clean run in the closing stages without having to find an extra gear from deep. The prominent and close-stalking profile is ideally suited to this shape on a flat 5f circuit with no pace collapse.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Forbidden Fades, Closers Nip
scenarios.trigger: If Forbidden's known tendency to fade in the finish sees it weaken sharply inside the last furlong, opening the door for runners who travelled well in midfield.
scenarios.body: Forbidden has been flagged as a fader and, even at a sustainable pace, a 5f sprint will expose that weakness late, creating a brief gap for midfield horses travelling with cover to swoop. Institute and Grande Cuvee, tracking comfortably, are ideally positioned to benefit as the leader drops away in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutants Deliver Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If Eager Lad or Tudor Flame arrive fit and forward enough on debut to produce a forward-travelling performance that catches the field cold.
scenarios.body: Unraced horses from the Oliver and Feane yards respectively carry complete unknown quantities, and on a fair-paced 5f track a well-schooled debutant who travels prominently can outrun their rivals before rivals can assess the threat. The lack of early pressure from genuine rivals means a forward-going newcomer faces minimal early interference.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Rout Field
scenarios.trigger: If pace genuinely collapses in the closing stages and the redistributed hold-up horses manage to close from their unnatural positions.
scenarios.body: Beach Barbie and White Smoke are genuine hold-up horses but are mapped into midfield due to the overcrowded rear of the field, meaning they are racing demonstrably out of role and must produce their best from a compromised position. This scenario is assigned low probability precisely because those horses are not operating in their natural slot and the single-leader tempo is unlikely to be fast enough to set up a true late sprint.

watchPoints.text: Forbidden — watch for whether it gets away cleanly and fully uncontested to the lead, as any early crowding or check that disrupts its rhythm could collapse the pace scenario the entire race shape is built upon.

Institute — Wayne Lordan is riding a horse with Dundalk synthetic form and a prominent style; watch its early positioning to confirm it settles just off Forbidden rather than getting trapped wide or shuffled back in the large 14-runner field.

White Smoke — Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking is significant given White Smoke's true hold-up style; watch whether the jockey opts to push forward early against the horse's natural tendency, which could signal the trainer expects a forward-going run today.

Grande Cuvee — Seamie Heffernan on a lightly raced 3yo with a third over this exact course configuration (5f, Curragh) is worth monitoring in the betting; any market confidence would elevate this runner's relevance materially.

Osterode — only one run but directly over 5f and fourth at the Curragh; Declan McDonogh is a shrewd booking and the visor worn last time suggests connections know what they are working with — monitor for any late money.

runners_data.name: Sir Les Patterson
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse who relies on a strong gallop to reel rivals in; 28 days since last run feels manageable, but sim-going figures (6/15 on Standard) are modest and the uncontested pace from Allsortz is a real concern for a closer of this type.

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Robson De Aguiar has had a reasonable 14-day strike-rate and Donagh O'Connor is a competent booking, but this 5yo hold-up performer's Standard-ground record (9/15) is uninspiring and a single leader up front is rarely what he needs.

runners_data.name: Black Forza
runners_data.note: 90 days off the track is the headline flag, and the tongue-tie switch adds a gear-change variable; naturally a hold-up type who was placed at 5f on Standard, but stepping back to 6f on Dundalk with a layoff of this length makes him hard to back confidently.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Blinkers applied and coming off a 5f Dundalk win on Standard — the sim-going form (1 win from 2 runs here) is the best in the race on this surface; however he is a hold-up type stepping up to 6f and will need more pace than Allsortz is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Recent form shows 113 before a pair of 30s, suggesting some regression; by nature a true hold-up runner who has been redistributed to midfield on the pace map — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects the reality that this race shape does not play to his strengths, and the 13-day turnaround warrants monitoring.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: An 8yo veteran with genuine Standard-ground placed form (3rd twice at 5f-6f on STA), but Ben Coen will find this horse racing forward of his natural position; the STYLE_FIT discount (0.92) is fair — he's a closer pushed up, and the uncontested front-running tempo is not the setup he wants.

runners_data.name: I Bid You Ajou
runners_data.note: A prominent-style handicapper who goes well at 6f and has recorded five consecutive placed efforts — the headgear note (p) and the Reese Holohan claim (7lb) are worth watching, but his 1/15 on Good sim-going limits confidence; the race shape here genuinely suits his style.

runners_data.name: Cuban Grey
runners_data.note: Ran just 6 days ago — fitness is not the concern, but freshness and recovery may be; a headgear-wearing hold-up type by instinct who has been redistributed forward on the map, and with 1 win from 4 on sim-going at 5f, stepping to 6f with a tight turnaround is a layered ask.

runners_data.name: Allsortz
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner and the single most important shape-setter in this race; David Marnane runners at Dundalk are worth noting, and Luke McAteer gets the call — three wins from 13 runs on sim-going (3/13) and a recent 6f placing suggests the trip is fine, but the OR of 82 off the front means rivals with superior ratings can close if he over-commits.

runners_data.name: Dandyville
runners_data.note: 376 days off the track is a glaring concern for this 8yo, and the recent form string (/7000-) tells a grim story; Chris Hayes is a capable partner, but a mare returning from a year's absence at this level needs everything to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up runner for David Marnane who ran 22 days ago — same trainer as Allsortz, which adds a yard-order dynamic; the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) reflects that being pushed into a midfield role blunts the closer's effectiveness, and a 2/5f win on Good last time was the only obvious positive in recent form.

runners_data.name: All The Girls
runners_data.note: Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim is a useful asset and the 5f Standard placing (3rd) suggests the surface suits; a prominent-style filly whose headgear (p) and OR of 76 means the weights help — she ran 8th and 6th on Good at 6f but the flat Dundalk track and prominent position in a controlled-pace race is a credible scenario for her profile.

races.paceDynamic: Allsortz is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 12-runner 6f Dundalk handicap and, with no other genuine pace horse to pressure them, Luke McAteer can dictate a comfortable, sustainable tempo from the front — this is a controlled, single-leader race shape rather than a contested gallop. The field carries significant hold-up bias, with Dark Ace, Collective Power, Fox In Flight, and Cuban Grey all natural rear-runners who are unlikely to secure their preferred position and will race closer to midfield than their instincts demand. I Bid You Ajou, Dandyville, and All The Girls offer some prominent cover behind Allsortz, but none has the pace to seriously challenge for the front. This race shape — a lone leader dictating a fair but uncontested tempo on a flat, standard-ground Dundalk track — strongly favours horses racing prominently or able to travel in the slipstream and produce a clean, sustained finish, rather than horses needing a strong pace collapse from the rear; the redistributed hold-up types face an uphill task racing out of their natural role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Allsortz Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Allsortz leads unchallenged and the pace is fair-but-sustainable, allowing a prominent racer to track and overhaul at the furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Allsortz sets a metronomic tempo on the front end, and the most effective challengers are those sitting just behind, travelling into the race — I Bid You Ajou and All The Girls, both prominent types, are ideally positioned to mount a challenge inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Allsortz Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace Allsortz sets proves slightly too slow for the closers to generate momentum, and the Marnane-trained 3yo simply outstays the field from the front.
scenarios.body: With no pressure early, Allsortz bowls along in front and never truly accelerates — the gap simply never closes as hold-up horses fail to get their preferred strong gallop.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace turns genuinely strong mid-race — perhaps I Bid You Ajou or Dandyville pushes up early — creating enough of a gallop for rear-runners to close.
scenarios.body: Dark Ace and Collective Power, if they can find a clear run from their redistributed midfield berths, carry the profile to rattle home late on a flat track — though their repositioned starting point materially reduces the likelihood.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches mid-race and jockeys get into trouble for room turning for home, creating an opening for a lightly-regarded runner to slip through.
scenarios.body: Sir Les Patterson or Black Forza, hold-up types with decent OR at the weights, could find daylight if the pace scenario falls apart and stragglers get in each other's way — a low-probability but non-zero route.

watchPoints.text: Allsortz — monitor how Luke McAteer settles the pace in the opening furlong; if he gets completely uncontested and sets a slow tempo, he becomes significantly harder to peg back and the entire race shape shifts toward a wire-to-wire outcome.

Dark Ace and Collective Power — both natural hold-up horses racing out of role in midfield; if the pace fails to quicken, watch for these two to find themselves without the strong gallop they need to unleash their finish, materially undermining their chances.

I Bid You Ajou — the 7lb claimer Reese Holohan may struggle to hold a prominent position in a 12-runner field if rivals push forward early; losing that prominent slot would cost this horse its primary tactical advantage in this race shape.

Dandyville — a 376-day absence for an 8yo at this level is significant; Chris Hayes will have the mare fit enough to run but any sign of greenness or weakness inside the final furlong would confirm she needs the run.

Black Forza — the 90-day layoff combined with a tongue-tie debut makes Dylan Browne McMonagle's instructions worth watching at the start; if the horse jumps cleanly and travels in the first half, the Standard-going placing form at 5f hints at ability on this surface.

runners_data.name: Never Mind Me
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner here after 683 days off; David Geraghty sends her out fresh into a race where her natural pace advantage is significant, but the long layoff from a horse carrying a STYLE_FIT flag means stamina reserves are unproven returning from such an absence.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Pat Foley's mare ran 2nd twice recently on similar going and is 1 from 6 in similar conditions; Luke McAteer takes over and she has a strong profile for a race where tracking the pace from second or third is the optimal route.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a finish fade flag; Hayes rides but the horse has placed just once in 15 starts on comparable going and a tendency to weaken in the closing stages makes this a difficult race shape to win from the back.

runners_data.name: Movin And Groovin
runners_data.note: Won most recently over this course and trip on standard going, giving his form strong relevance here — though his true hold-up style means he's been pushed forward on the map; the 34-day break is fine and Marnane's runners carry the REDISTRIBUTED caveat, so his natural late run may be compromised by the crowded midfield.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on standard at Dundalk last time and steps to a mile; Dylan Browne McMonagle is a strong book, and the horse has shown enough close-finishing form to be dangerous if he gets daylight, despite only 3 wins-or-places from 15 comparable starts.

runners_data.name: Queen Leila
runners_data.note: Five runs all on standard going at Dundalk, winning over a mile and placed twice over seven furlongs on the same surface — outstanding course and going form; Patrick McGettigan (5lb) is the rider and she is equipped with tongue-tie, making her a high-fit runner for this specific race shape.

runners_data.name: Reponse Finale
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell saddles her just three days after her last run, which raises freshness questions; the horse is a true hold-up type re-mapped to midfield, and her best form came over 10f, suggesting stamina rather than speed is her tool — not ideal over this shorter mile.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: A legitimate prominent racer who can challenge for a forward position early; McCourt's seven-year-old has three wins-or-places from 15 similar runs and headgear (tv) may sharpen focus, but finishing unplaced in recent outings questions whether he can sustain a challenge once tackled.

runners_data.name: Tenacious
runners_data.note: Mrs Harrington's three-year-old carries a fade flag and a REDISTRIBUTED note, both pointing the same direction — likely to be swamped in the midfield pack and unable to produce a telling late effort; Foley is a strong jockey booking but the horse is 0 from 9 on similar or comparable going.

runners_data.name: Beau Army
runners_data.note: Won most recently for McGuinness and has hit the frame repeatedly in defeat; fitted with a visor and returning eight days later, his natural hold-up style is compressed here, but his recent winning run and tactical versatility give him an each-way profile if he can find a clear lane.

runners_data.name: Misava
runners_data.note: Three consecutive fade finishes in the form string, confirmed by the finish-fade flag; the hold-up style is honest but she has posted zero wins or places from her four comparable-going runs and there is no evidence she can sustain a run into this congested finish.

runners_data.name: Cause I Like You
runners_data.note: Joyce's 3lb claim may help this horse's raw ability show — she won on good and placed twice, showing she can finish; but 0 wins from 14 runs on comparable conditions and the REDISTRIBUTED caveat for her true style dampen expectations for a big run.

runners_data.name: Master Garvey
runners_data.note: Declan McDonogh takes the ride and the horse placed 3rd over 10f recently, suggesting he stays but may lack the pace to challenge over a flat Dundalk mile; the REDISTRIBUTED tag reflects that his hold-up style will be squeezed in a very full midfield.

runners_data.name: Six Wings
runners_data.note: A prominent racer who has shown a consistent fade pattern across recent starts over 8-11f; Leigh Roche and Paul Flynn have had no winners in 21 days and the horse has posted six placing-free runs in the last six outings — hard to trust here.

runners_data.name: Due In June
runners_data.note: The fade flag is consistent with five consecutive finishes between 6th and 9th; she is a genuine hold-up horse nudged into midfield on the map, and with no jockey named yet, trainer form flat, and no win or place at comparable conditions, she is difficult to support.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Edward Lynam sends out this hold-up mare with a finish-fade flag and a blinkered headgear note; her one run on standard going at Dundalk produced a 5th, which is the best comparable result in her book, but 20-runner field losses at shorter trips suggest she's likely to fill the rear half here.

runners_data.name: Polanco
runners_data.note: Five zeros in the recent form string and a route through 12f, 8f, 6f and 5f distances reveals no consistency; the REDISTRIBUTED and fade flags combine with a trainer at 0 wins in 14 days and 0 comparable wins to make this the most difficult runner to make a case for.

races.paceDynamic: Never Mind Me is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-runner field and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, should be allowed to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on the Dundalk polytrack-style standard surface over one mile. Rampage and Six Wings are the only other prominent-style runners, but neither carries the profile or the trainer momentum to seriously challenge for the early lead, meaning Never Mind Me can dictate a measured, uncontested tempo. With so many genuine hold-up horses — Tenacious, Movin And Groovin, Beau Army, Reponse Finale, Cause I Like You, Master Garvey, Polanco, and Due In June among them — all compressed into the midfield section due to the structural imbalance of this race, the true closers cannot get daylight early and will be forced to work harder than ideal to find room in the straight. This race shape heavily favours horses who can travel close to the uncontested pace or who have proven ability to produce a sustained, rather than a sharp late, finish — making handy-travelling prominent types and horses that can sit just off the leader the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Never Mind Me Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Never Mind Me is permitted to dictate an honest but unforced gallop from the front with Rampage and Six Wings unable or unwilling to apply pressure.
scenarios.body: Never Mind Me sets a rhythm that suits herself perfectly, and the compressed midfield traffic means closers cannot deliver a clean late run; a horse tracking in second or third with a forward position locked in from the outset has the clearest passage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and horses with a clean line through from just off midfield arrive with momentum in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Famous Enough and Queen Leila, both proven at this track and trip on standard going, are ideally suited to sitting just off the pace and producing a clean late challenge; the compressed field means those with course craft and a clear run benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Fades, Surging Late
scenarios.trigger: If Never Mind Me sets a stronger pace than intended or tires late, opening a gap for hold-up horses who thread through the congested midfield.
scenarios.body: Movin And Groovin and Beau Army, though mapped in midfield due to the hold-up surplus, are genuine winning types whose recent form shows late-race ability if given space; the traffic risk is real but a clear run could allow one to finish powerfully.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Leader Gifts Win
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches tightly at a dawdle and Never Mind Me steals the race on the bridle without being challenged through the early stages.
scenarios.body: Never Mind Me, allowed to control fractions entirely without acceleration from rivals, simply extends the lead into the straight before tired hold-up horses can close the gap; a truly gifted front-running performance from a horse whose long absence is offset by her natural positional dominance today.

watchPoints.text: Never Mind Me sets the entire pace dynamic — if she is allowed to stride clear unchallenged in the first quarter, she could be very difficult to peg back and all positional assessments hinge on her early speed.

The compression of multiple hold-up horses (Tenacious, Beau Army, Movin And Groovin, Reponse Finale, Cause I Like You, Polanco, Due In June) into the midfield creates a significant traffic and interference risk in the straight — runners who cannot find daylight by the two-furlong pole will likely finish empty.

Queen Leila's course-and-distance form on standard going at Dundalk is notably strong — five runs, one win, two placings — and if she is allowed to travel wide and unimpeded, her profile makes her a serious danger to the field regardless of the pace shape.

Beau Army returns just eight days after his last run for a trainer (McGuinness) whose horses hit the frame regularly despite the short turnaround; monitor market moves to gauge if connections believe the quick return is a positive rather than a concern.

Rampage wearing a tongue-tie and visor combination is worth noting as a potential pace influence — if he pushes up aggressively to join Never Mind Me, even briefly, the tempo could lift and alter the scenario probabilities materially in favour of hold-up finishers.

runners_data.name: Iron Fist
runners_data.note: The de facto pacesetter by default — Mrs Harrington's four-year-old has strong 10f form including a recent win and two places on Good, but steps up slightly in trip here; 35 days off the track and a style-fit flag (mapped Prominent, historically a Leader) means its chance depends on how well it handles the front-running role it will be pushed into.

runners_data.name: Apercu
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with headgear (blinkers) who will race off the back of the field; no wins or placed efforts on comparable going from 15 similar-ground starts is a significant concern, and six-year-old has been patchy in form (48027) suggesting a confidence effort rather than a banker selection.

runners_data.name: Genoah
runners_data.note: Travels well from off the pace in the tongue-plate and has the best synthetic/standard-equivalent record in the field (8 wins/places from 15 similar-ground runs); 12 days since last run is a slight freshness flag but the O'Callaghan handler is in decent 14-day form (2/14).

runners_data.name: Star Harbour
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old with excellent recent distance form — two seconds from four starts at 12f on Good — who will press for a prominent position; the visor is a positive for concentration and McDonogh's booking lends confidence, though 3 days since last run is aggressive scheduling.

runners_data.name: Touch The Moon
runners_data.note: Won over 16f on Good last time out and is effectively stepping back in trip; the Durkan yard is cold (0/6 in 14 days) and the horse has only one placing on comparable going from 15 such starts, so pace shape will need to be strongly in its favour.

runners_data.name: Crypto Force
runners_data.note: 112-day layoff is the dominant factor — a long absence on the handicap mark (87) with headgear (cheekpieces) added; has placed form on standard ground at Dundalk (5/10f/STA) and holds his own over the trip but needs to come back to something close to peak fitness.

runners_data.name: Tribal Star
runners_data.note: True hold-up type with headgear (cheekpieces) who has placed at an extraordinary distance (2/17f/GOO) and won on standard going at Dundalk (1/11-14f range); the wide draw concern is neutral at Dundalk's flat track, and Caffrey is an apprentice booking worth noting in a large field.

runners_data.name: Slieve Binnian
runners_data.note: Has failed to find the frame in all five recent starts and all previous form is over shorter distances than today's 1m2½f — the horse is stepping up significantly in trip and all Dundalk standard-ground experience (2 from 15) has been over sprint/mile trips, making this a risky distance-stretch.

runners_data.name: Beauparc
runners_data.note: Heffernan takes the ride on a horse with genuine placed form at 12-13f on Good (two seconds), but this is a natural hold-up performer being pushed forward by field congestion — its best chance comes only if the race is truly honest and it can find a clean outside run late in the Dundalk straight.

runners_data.name: Follow Me
runners_data.note: Ridden by the high-profile McMonagle booking, but a 46-day break and recent form reading 04-983 is unencouraging; this horse's natural hold-up style (headgear: visor) is compromised by the packed midfield it will likely be channelled into, and shorter-trip form (7-8f runs feature heavily) raises a stamina query at 1m2½f.

runners_data.name: Steel Cut
runners_data.note: Has a single placing on standard going from five tries (2/10f/STA) and wears blinkers; at OR 79 with a 26-day gap, the Oliver yard (2/10 in 14 days) is the main positive angle — but as a true hold-up type forced into midfield by field dynamics, its best form requires a free run from the rear that is unlikely to materialise cleanly.

runners_data.name: Quatre Bras
runners_data.note: Strong handicap record in terms of sheer place-strikes (2 wins, 5 places from 15 comparable-going starts) but all that form has come over 7-8f on Good — stepping up markedly to 1m2½f on a very different surface is a significant leap, and its redistribution from natural hold-up to midfield further complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Cala Bonita
runners_data.note: Lightly raced four-year-old filly with a win on Soft and placed efforts at 12-13f — the extra distance and standard ground are unknowns but she's trending positively (form: -48471 shows a placing last time); Joyce's 3lb claim helps in a competitive handicap and she could outrun her OR 76 rating if travel holds.

runners_data.name: Nermal
runners_data.note: The trainer-jockey combination is the same person (Andrew Slattery), which is an intriguing angle; the three-year-old has strong placed form at 10-12f on Good and standard going (2/10f/GOO, 2/8f/STA) and arrives 19 days fresh — a prominent horse with the tactical speed to sit right behind the leader and strike.

races.paceDynamic: Iron Fist is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 1m2½f Dundalk standard-ground trip — a shape that suits a patient, measured performance rather than an attritional slog. Star Harbour, Touch The Moon, Slieve Binnian, Cala Bonita and Nermal will press for prominent positions behind Iron Fist, meaning the early positions from second to fifth will be genuinely contested, with the field compressing into a tight bunch through the middle stages. The hold-up contingent — Apercu, Genoah, Crypto Force, Tribal Star — will have natural cover and room to manoeuvre from the rear, but several horses tagged as true hold-up types (Steel Cut, Follow Me, Beauparc, Quatre Bras) are unlikely to find their natural rearward position given the volume of midfield traffic and will end up shuffled closer than ideal. With one uncontested leader setting a fair but not punishing pace, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently just off the lead and produce a sustained finish in the straight — a tactical premium placed firmly on prominent racers with good Dundalk/synthetic-equivalent form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Iron Fist sets an uncontested, even gallop and prominent horses traveling fluidly behind him quicken past in the straight.
scenarios.body: Iron Fist's lone leader role means the pace is honest but not severe, creating a race that sets up ideally for horses travelling second to fourth and kicking from the two-furlong pole; the standard going rewards those with tactical speed rather than pure stamina. Nermal and Star Harbour are the natural beneficiaries — both proven prominent racers at this sort of trip who can sit just off the pace and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group go too hard chasing Iron Fist and the pace quickens mid-race, burning off the front-runners and leaving the true closers to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Apercu and Genoah, both genuine hold-up types with sound form over course-relevant distances on comparable ground, would have the acceleration to sweep past a tiring prominent pack in the final furlong; Genoah's strong synthetic-equivalent record (8 wins/places from 15) makes it especially well-placed in this shape. The key is pace collapse at the head of affairs, which is possible if Star Harbour or Touch The Moon press Iron Fist earlier than expected.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a falsely slow pace that suddenly heats up in the home straight, producing a messy, compressed finish.
scenarios.body: A stop-start gallop where multiple horses hit the front together at the two-furlong pole scrambles form lines and opens the door for horses with residual fresh energy like Quatre Bras or Beauparc — both redistributed from their natural hold-up berth but carrying tactical fitness; the compressed field means any horse with a clear run could grab a slice. This shape is discounted because it relies on redistributed runners performing ideally from a position they are unlikely to naturally secure.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Iron Fist Wires the Field
scenarios.trigger: If Iron Fist is allowed a complete, unchallenged lead and the pace is so controlled that no hold-up or prominent rival can close the gap in the short Dundalk straight.
scenarios.body: At 1m2½f on standard ground with no pressure applied, a class-loaded front-runner dictating every fraction can simply outstay rivals who are never asked a question early enough; Iron Fist's recent winning form (1/10f/SOF, 2/10f/GOO) shows it can deliver at this trip when producing its best. This scenario is the least probable given Iron Fist's style-fit caveat (racing out of role at P rather than its natural L) and the depth of quality chasing it home.

watchPoints.text: Watch Iron Fist's early fractions — if it is allowed to coast through the first half-mile at a tempo well below what this field needs, the race becomes a sprint finish from 2f out and the prominent pack behind may simply lack the finishing kick to reel it in cleanly.

Star Harbour races just 3 days after its last start — monitor if it shows any signs of staleness or flat in the parade ring, as tiredness late in a 1m2½f contest on a tight turnaround could compromise a horse that needs to be travelling powerfully into the straight.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up horses (Steel Cut, Follow Me, Beauparc, Quatre Bras) will all be jockeying for a similar midfield berth — watch for crowding and checking on the first bend as none of them will naturally want to be there, creating a collision-risk flashpoint.

Nermal's trainer-jockey identity (Slattery trains and rides) means stable instructions and race-day execution are perfectly aligned — watch for an aggressive move to press Iron Fist early if Slattery judges the pace too slow, which would fundamentally reshape the race dynamic.

Genoah (tongue-plate, 12 days since last run) has the best record in similar going conditions in the field — watch how Leigh Roche positions it in the first quarter-mile; if Genoah gets a clear sight of the leaders from sixth or seventh by halfway, it represents the primary late threat to the prominent group.

races.name: Friday Night Lights Return Weekly From 18th September Handicap

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Adrian McGuinness who has placed twice on Standard going at this trip; headgear visor suggests he needs restraining, and the fade flag is a real concern over 1m2½f, but if he tracks Coul Dore's soft lead he gets the ideal setup — his 9-day turnaround suggests freshness over fitness.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse with a modest 1-from-7 strike rate on Standard going and only one career win; fade flag is a concern and the step up beyond 8f in recent form raises questions about whether this trip is within his comfort zone.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Prominent-style runner who has placed at 11f on Good going and handles step-up in trip; Patrick McGettigan (5lb claim) is a useful booking and the 29-day break is not a concern — this horse's natural racing position puts it in prime tactical ground behind Coul Dore.

runners_data.name: Anchors Away
runners_data.note: Hold-up type wearing a tongue-tie for the first time; has placed twice at 10f on Standard, but the fade flag and a 37-day absence temper enthusiasm, even though the form line showing a 3rd and 4th at this course on Standard is superficially appealing.

runners_data.name: Storm Eric
runners_data.note: The most credible hold-up performer in this field given four placings from five recent starts at 10f on Standard going — this horse genuinely suits the surface and trip, and Adam Grant's 7lb claim stretches the value; represents the primary threat from off the pace if the race develops as a late-run affair.

runners_data.name: Tortola
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (hood) and is a natural closer; this race shape doesn't favour the rear of the field and its STYLE_FIT flag reflects the difficulty of getting a clear run in a 17-horse field when forced to race further forward than usual — fade history compounds the concern.

runners_data.name: Copper Craft
runners_data.note: Blinkered hold-up horse whose two recent 2nd-place finishes came at 10f on Going to Good and 12f on Standard — useful course form — but mapped to midfield rather than its natural berth, which will require the horse to adapt its rhythm; trainer A Oliver has 2 from 10 in the 14-day window.

runners_data.name: Retro Gal
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for Henry De Bromhead wearing blinkers; only one start at Dundalk (7th on Standard at 8f), and the bulk of her form is on Good/Soft — Standard going is an unknown quantity, making her a difficult proposition to assess.

runners_data.name: Barretstown
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who has won twice and placed three times from 15 career starts at Dundalk at 10f on Standard — the course-and-distance form is the headline; however, the 71-day break, OR of just 46, and redistribution from his natural hold-up berth make it hard to construct a winning case.

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: Fitted with a tongue-tie, this mare has all her recent form at Dundalk on Standard but fails to win (0 from 11 on sim-going) and has consistently finished mid-pack at 8f-12f; the redistribution from her true hold-up role is an additional complication in a 17-runner field.

runners_data.name: Coul Dore
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner and key pace-setter; Seamie Heffernan's booking is significant for this grade, but the horse carries a clear fade flag and has not won on Standard going — the lack of pace rivals is its greatest asset and the question is whether it can conserve enough for the closing stages after 56 days off.

runners_data.name: Shahada Ace
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have produced finishes outside the top five on Good going, and the horse has no Standard-going record listed — a first-time Dundalk starter on this surface who faces a stiff task making up ground from a true hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Wingit
runners_data.note: Three-year-old fitted with a tongue-tie whose best effort was a 2nd over 13f on Good; the redistribution from a deeper hold-up position is problematic in a full field, and the absence of any Standard-going wins or places across five relevant starts limits confidence.

runners_data.name: Threebiggulps
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with an OR of just 40 and a best recent finish of 9th — the form is plainly insufficient at this level, and the horse's hold-up tendency in a crowded field where it cannot settle in its natural position makes this a very difficult race.

runners_data.name: Yquem
runners_data.note: Won over 9f on Good going recently and placed in a 10f Good race too — the form represents live claims; the redistribution from its preferred hold-up spot is a mild concern but Yquem's recent trajectory (1-3-3-4 sequence) suggests it is in a productive vein and is one of the better-credentialled hold-up types in the race.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Boy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old for H Rogers, wearing a hood, with a consistent run of unplaced efforts on Good going — all form on Good rather than Standard, and the 14-day turnaround alongside a fade flag means this horse needs to find significantly more than its recent efforts suggest.

runners_data.name: Without Love
runners_data.note: Natural closer with two recent 2nd-place finishes at 12f on Standard and a win at the same trip — the going and distance profile is genuinely strong; mapped to midfield rather than its preferred position, but of all the redistributed hold-up types this one has the most convincing evidence it can still be competitive on this surface if things fall right.

races.paceDynamic: Coul Dore is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-horse field and, crucially, faces no genuine pressure from another pace horse — this means Seamie Heffernan can dictate a controlled, sustainable tempo around Dundalk's flat polytrack configuration at 1m2½f. The absence of a rival to challenge Coul Dore early creates a soft lead scenario: moderate fractions, a compressed mid-race pack, and a sprint-style finish from the home turn. Dancing Steve and Rising Sky are the only realistic prominent horses capable of tracking the front-runner, placing them in the best tactical position to pounce if Coul Dore fades — which its finishing-fade flag suggests is a genuine risk. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up types: Tortola, Without Love, Copper Craft, Barretstown, My Vonnie, Wingit, Shahada Ace, Yquem and Threebiggulps are all true closers redistributed to midfield on the map simply because the race shape cannot accommodate them all at the rear; of these, Storm Eric and Without Love have the most convincing Dundalk/standard-going profiles to make meaningful ground. The pace shape overwhelmingly favours a prominent racer tracking a soft lead — specifically, any horse that can sit second or third without burning energy early and then sustain a run through the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Soft Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore bowls along unchallenged at a comfortable gallop and one or two prominent trackers sit just behind before striking turning in.
scenarios.body: Coul Dore's fade flag means the race will be there for a prominent horse who conserves energy through the middle portion and hits the front 1f-2f out; the compressed field then finishes in a tight bunch but the prominent racer has first run. Dancing Steve and Rising Sky are ideally positioned to execute this pattern, with Rising Sky's recent 3rd at 11f on Good a legitimate prep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Coul Dore Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Coul Dore's jockey Seamie Heffernan (a significant booking for this grade) drops the pace sufficiently low that the horse's fade tendency is masked.
scenarios.body: A truly dawdling gallop at this trip can allow even a known fader to hit a flat spot and respond when shaken up; the 56-day absence is a concern but Crawford's runners often arrive fresh. With no rival forcing the issue, the lead could translate into a winning one if the field gets too far back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough to compress the field into a mass finish, allowing a horse coming from mid-pack to pick off tiring rivals late.
scenarios.body: Storm Eric's consistent Dundalk profile — four top-three finishes in five recent starts at 10f on Standard — makes it the most credible beneficiary, as it tends to travel powerfully in running and needs only modest improvement on a track it clearly favours. Without Love also has two recent 2nd-place finishes at 12f on Standard and stays well, but both are racing in positions closer to their natural style than many redistributed rivals.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If a surprise secondary mover pushes Coul Dore harder than expected in the early stages, causing an unsustainably quick early tempo.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace collapse is unlikely given the lone front-runner scenario, but if it occurs the true hold-up horses deep in the field get their race; Storm Eric and Yquem — the latter showing a win and a placed effort in recent Goodwood form — would be best placed to finish off a ragged race. Most redistributed hold-up types would still lack the natural rhythm of their preferred position.

watchPoints.text: Storm Eric has posted four top-three finishes in five recent runs at 10f on Standard going — if the pace is controlled and the field concertinas, this horse is the clearest non-prominent danger in the race.

Coul Dore's fade flag is the central risk to the most-likely scenario: if Seamie Heffernan over-quickens even marginally in a 17-horse race, the front-runner could capitulate inside the final furlong and hand the race to a prominent tracker.

With nine genuine hold-up types competing for the same closing ground, traffic at Dundalk's relatively tight home turn is a real possibility — watch for horses like Yquem and Without Love getting checked or switched wide in the final two furlongs.

Rising Sky's prominent style and course experience make it worth monitoring in the betting: if the market moves in its favour before the off, it likely reflects informed money on the race being run to suit a prominent tracker.

The 17-runner field and a single front-runner create compressed mid-race conditions — any horse drawn wide that settles prominently early (Dancing Steve in particular) could dictate its own fate by bridging the gap to Coul Dore before the turn.
